<sub><sup>(message by IssueLinks)</sup></sub>

Hey there @bdraco, mind taking a look at this issue as it has been labeled with an integration (`hunterdouglas_powerview`) you are listed as a [code owner](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/CODEOWNERS#L455) for? Thanks!
<sub><sup>(message by CodeOwnersMention)</sup></sub>

I have this issue too, had shades installed yesterday. 
They get out of sync when the shades are moved via the powerview app or remote. 
Ideally the intergration should poll the API to keep in sync. But sounds like that might drain the battery powered blinds.

The two other ideas would be, ignore state and send commands to open/close regardless. Or fetch the state before running commands to make sure scenes operate correctly

We report only what the hub reports

There is an api to force it to update the state and sync with the shade, but we do not do forced polling because it will drain many of battery powered ones in a matter of days and takes up anywhere from 5-90 seconds per shade.

There currently is no reliable way to tell if a device is battery powered or not.

Well if I operate my blinds from home assistant from all up to alll down. It updates the state half way. But when the blind is closed in reality home assistant state that its half way open. This never happens when you do it from the power view app or HomeKit(not via home assistant bridge)

Thats a bug in the timing code for devices that take longer than [30s](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/dev/homeassistant/components/hunterdouglas_powerview/cover.py#L46) to complete an operation. If it takes longer to operate than expected so it refreshes the state too soon, and since we never force poll again it never updates since the hub doesn't ever update its internal state without a forced refresh for some devices.

That code really needs to be moved to the upstream `aiopvapi` library, but since previous PRs took months to merge, this isn't something that could happen quickly.

I only have two of these devices (both the same) so there isn't much I can do improve the use cases for the other hardware.

This integration really needs someone with access to wider variety of these devices to take over the upstream library, as well as be a codeowner on the Home Assistant side.

> I only have two of these devices (both the same) so there isn't much I can do improve the use cases for the other hardware.
> 
> This integration really needs someone with access to wider variety of these devices to take over the upstream library, as well as be a codeowner on the Home Assistant side.

Im happy to help you with testing if you wanna modify the update timers.

One solution could be to force poll every few seconds until it gets to the expected state with some type of timeout if it never does reach it.  

Changing the timer really isn't the solution here as the entire logic is predicated on assuming we can correctly guess how long the device will take to open/close/complete the operation.  Since it is different for every device it is almost always going to make a bad guess.  This logic needs to be ripped out and new logic needs to be done in the `aiopvapi` library.

> One solution could be to force poll every few seconds until it gets to the expected state with some type of timeout if it never does reach it.

I'm working with my integrator to put pressure on them, I spent a lot of money and if HunterD can't get a flipping basic API to work then they can remove them all and I'll use zwave blinds...

[Using API commands UserData-Shades-Scenes.pdf](https://github.com/home-assistant/core/files/8501924/Using.API.commands.UserData-Shades-Scenes.pdf)

So I think one bug from HA still exists, I don't think HA should stop the user from sending up/down commands based on it's internal state. If I have a scene with everything as down, even if HA thinks they are down, it should still send the down command (yeah thats dumb, but thanks HD!).

I just had a long conversation with an integration tech at Hunter Douglass, TLDR; don't buy their stuff, just find something with ZWave (Bali/Graber/Somfy/etc).

Two things came out of that call:

1. They don't care about their integrators - Even the Apple Home Kit team gave up trying to integrate fully with there stuff. (If thats not telling not sure what is)
2. Remotes cause the problems:
- Their remotes don't talk through the PowerView hub, so once you use that, PowerView has no idea what state the blinds are.
- Don't send commands at them unless you need to you'll nuke the battery (looks like HA does this already, based on the state from PV)
- Do poll the state of the unit for battery while it's moving, as that gives a better state of charge.(Looks like your change to poll until it's static is fine).


The tech couldn't remember, but one potential would be make to make the polling <15 seconds if the unit is still in motion as he mentioned the radio goes to sleep after ~15 seconds, so closer to blind being stationary the more battery friendly it is. (If it's hard wired, then who cares).

He's going to follow up about units not reporting battery or hardwired status correctly as that does sound like a bug from the sounds of it.
